source_text: Nec a lege ostensum est vel ostendi potuit, quia numquam legislator usque ad hanc veniret amentiam, ut praeciperet cuiquam: Noli ita vel ita nasci; et quod admoneri non decuit, ut corrigatur, iustum esse non potest, ut puniatur.
pass_a_gloss: Nor has it been shown by the law or could it have been shown, because a lawgiver would never come even to this madness, that he would command anyone: Do not be born thus or thus; and what it was not fitting to be warned so that it may be corrected cannot be just that it be punished.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Nor was it revealed by the law, nor could it have been. No lawgiver would ever reach such madness as to command anyone, ‘Do not be born this way or that.’ And where it would be inappropriate to give a warning so that something may be corrected, it cannot be just to impose punishment.

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
